findings.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77 — Role/client/group removal cleanup listener is now gated on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) instead of ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 used by management()/evaluator() elsewhere in this file, so setPermissionsEnabled(...) cleanup is skipped entirely (a regression from previously unconditional execution) when only V2 FGAP is enabled

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:326 — No test exercises MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE / canMapClientScopeRoles; testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient only covers MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, so ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles (services/.../ClientPermissionsV2.java:101-102) is entirely untested despite being a new scope added to the CLIENTS resource type

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:126 — No test creates a second realm to verify the new isAdminSameRealm() guard (also at lines 208, 238) actually prevents a permission granted in realm A from applying to clients in realm B; this security-relevant cross-realm scoping check ships without a regression test

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:250 — The dynamically created "newClient" in testManageAllClients is removed only by an explicit mid-test call, not registered via realm.cleanup() or handled in @AfterEach onAfter() (line 79); if an assertion before that removal call fails, the client leaks into the realm and can break subsequent test runs (e.g. duplicate clientId conflict)

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:326 — No test exercises MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE / canMapClientScopeRoles; testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient only covers MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, so ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles (services/.../ClientPermissionsV2.java:101-102) is entirely untested despite being a new scope added to the CLIENTS resource type

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new scope constant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` to `AdminPermissionsSchema` and includes it in the `CLIENTS` resource type scopes. It also adds new logic in `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` which checks `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`. In the updated/added tests, `PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` grants only `MAP_ROLES`, `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`, and `CONFIGURE` on the client (no `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`), and there is no other test in the shown diff that exercises granting/denying `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` or calling behavior that would specifically validate `canMapClientScopeRoles`. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap for newly added authorization scope logic, not a direct functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:126 — No test creates a second realm to verify the new isAdminSameRealm() guard (also at lines 208, 238) actually prevents a permission granted in realm A from applying to clients in realm B; this security-relevant cross-realm scoping check ships without a regression test

adjudication.rationale: ClientPermissionsV2 introduces new authorization gates that explicitly depend on cross-realm scoping via `if (!root.isAdminSameRealm()) return false;` in `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` and `hasPermission(String)` (around lines ~170 and ~206 in the new file). The added/modified tests (e.g., `PermissionClientTest`, `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest`) only operate within a single managed realm (`@InjectAdminClient(mode = MANAGED_REALM, ...)`) and do not create or exercise a second realm to prove permissions from realm A cannot affect realm B. Given this new realm-boundary guard is security-relevant, the absence of a regression test for cross-realm isolation is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern, but not a verifiable defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:250 — The dynamically created "newClient" in testManageAllClients is removed only by an explicit mid-test call, not registered via realm.cleanup() or handled in @AfterEach onAfter() (line 79); if an assertion before that removal call fails, the client leaks into the realm and can break subsequent test runs (e.g. duplicate clientId conflict)

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest.testManageAllClients, a client with clientId "newClient" is created after granting MANAGE via createAllPermission, and later deleted via an explicit mid-test remove() call. The @AfterEach onAfter() in this class only deletes scope permissions (permissions.findAll(...).remove()), not realm clients. There is no realm.cleanup() registration for the created client. Therefore, if the test fails between the create and the explicit remove (e.g., an assertion on the created client), the created client can leak into the realm and potentially break subsequent runs due to duplicate clientId conflicts.
